Confidence Intervals for the Difference of Two Poisson Rates

Source: R/poissonDiffCI.R
poissonDiffCI.Rd

Computes a confidence interval for the difference \(x_1/n_1 - x_2/n_2\) of two independent Poisson rates.

poissonDiffCI(
  x1,
  n1 = 1,
  x2,
  n2 = 1,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  sides = c("two.sided", "left", "right"),
  method = c("mover", "wald")
)

Arguments

x1

number of events in the first sample

n1

time base for the first event count

x2

number of events in the second sample

n2

time base for the second event count

conf.level

confidence level, defaults to 0.95

sides

a character string specifying the side of the confidence interval, one of "two.sided" (default), "left" or "right"

method

character string specifying the method, either "mover" (default) or "wald"

Value

If recycling yields a single case, a named numeric vector with elements est, lci and uci. Otherwise a data frame with one row per case, whose first three columns are est, lci and uci and whose remaining columns contain the recycled argument values.

Details

"mover" (default) applies the method of variance estimates recovery of Zou and Donner (2008): exact Garwood limits are obtained for each rate separately and recombined, which keeps the interval close to nominal coverage even for small counts. "wald" uses the asymptotic normal approximation and degenerates to zero width when both counts are zero.

Arguments are recycled to a common length. sides names the side carrying the finite limit: "left" yields \([lci, \infty)\) and "right" yields \((-\infty, uci]\), with the full error probability placed on that one side.

References

Zou, G. Y., Donner, A. (2008) Construction of confidence limits about effect measures: a general approach. Statistics in Medicine, 27(10), 1693-1702.

See also

poissonCI, poissonRatioCI, binomDiffCI

Other ci.proportion: binomCI(), binomDiffCI(), binomRatioCI(), multinomCI(), poissonCI(), poissonRatioCI()

Examples

## 15 events in 100 person-years against 6 events in 120 person-years
poissonDiffCI(15, 100, 6, 120)
#>        est        lci        uci 
#> 0.10000000 0.01155263 0.20241565 
## [1] est 0.10000000 lci 0.01155263 uci 0.20241565

poissonDiffCI(15, 100, 6, 120, method = "wald")
#>        est        lci        uci 
#> 0.10000000 0.01419326 0.18580674 

## recycling returns one row per case
poissonDiffCI(x1 = c(15, 20), n1 = 100, x2 = 6, n2 = 120)
#>    est        lci       uci x1  n1 x2  n2 conf.level
#> 1 0.10 0.01155263 0.2024156 15 100  6 120       0.95
#> 2 0.15 0.05243411 0.2633907 20 100  6 120       0.95
